items.stem: To limit pod-to-pod traffic to only what is required, what should you apply first?

options.text: A default-deny NetworkPolicy, then allow required flows
options.rationale: Correct: default-deny then explicit allow enforces least privilege.

options.text: A LoadBalancer service for every pod
options.rationale: Exposing pods widely increases, not reduces, risk.

options.text: Disabling the API server audit log
options.rationale: Disabling auditing reduces visibility, not exposure.

items.explanation: Correct: default-deny then explicit allow enforces least privilege.

items.stem: Which approach best ensures only trusted images run in the cluster?

options.text: Admission control that verifies image signatures/digests
options.rationale: Correct: admission-time verification blocks untrusted images.
Tags are mutable; 'latest' can change under you.

options.text: Allowing any image from any registry

options.rationale: Running as root worsens, not improves, security.

items.explanation: Correct: admission-time verification blocks untrusted images.

items.stem: Which TWO reduce a node's attack surface? (Select TWO)

options.rationale: Correct: fewer installed services means fewer vulnerabilities.

options.text: Apply a seccomp profile to restrict syscalls
options.rationale: Correct: seccomp limits the syscalls a workload can make.
Privileged workloads expand the attack surface.

options.text: Open all firewall ports for convenience

items.explanation: Correct: fewer installed services means fewer vulnerabilities. Correct: seccomp limits the syscalls a workload can make.
